For F>0 Markov bounds the chance of exceeding εF by 1/e; independence makes the probability that every row exceeds it at most e^(−d)≤δ. Unlike explicit candidate cancellation, this stores hashed aggregate counters and answers a supplied key query. No empirical benefit or implementation is claimed.

source.citation: Bloom (1970), Space/time trade-offs in hash coding with allowable errors, Communications of the ACM 13(7), 422–426, Method 2, p. 423. DOI 10.1145/362686.362692. https://crystal.uta.edu/~mcguigan/cse6350/papers/Bloom.pdf ; conditional occupancy ratio independently derived

mechanism_note: Inserted keys retain every addressed bit by monotonicity. Under independent uniform distinct query addresses, exactly choose(T,k) of choose(m,k) equally likely subsets lie wholly in the occupied set. This is conditional on the bit pattern and differs from the common independent-with-replacement approximation. Boolean set-membership screening differs from Count–Min numerical frequency estimation.

source.citation: Charikar, Chen and Farach-Colton (2002), Finding frequent items in data streams, ICALP, LNCS 2380, 693–703, sections 3.2, 4 and 4.2. DOI 10.1007/3-540-45465-9_59. https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/spring04/cos598B/bib/CharikarCF.pdf ; fixed-query signed L2 bound independently derived

mechanism_note: Expand Z_j−f_x as Σ_{y≠x} f_y s_j(x)s_j(y)1{h_j(y)=h_j(x)}. Independent unbiased pairwise signs cancel cross terms since s_j(x)²=1; uniform pairwise bucket hashes yield the stated variance. Chebyshev bounds a bad row by 1/4 and Hoeffding bounds a majority of bad independent rows by exp(−d/8). Signed collision cancellation and median estimation differ from nonnegative minimum estimation.

source.citation: Flajolet, Fusy, Gandouet and Meunier (2007), HyperLogLog: the analysis of a near-optimal cardinality estimation algorithm, DMTCS proceedings AH, 137–156, section 1, equation (3), Theorem 1 and section 4, Figure 3. DOI 10.46298/dmtcs.3545. https://dmtcs.episciences.org/en/articles/3545/download

mechanism_note: Maxima make repeated identical hashes idempotent and ensure that componentwise maximum of compatible states equals the state obtained from their union. Under independent uniform hashes, each register is empty with probability (1−1/m)^n; the small-range logarithm approximates inversion of the resulting expected empty count. The finite-range logarithm analogously inverts expected hash occupancy approximately. Neither inversion is an exact unbiased estimate. The original practical program uses zero initialization, unlike the analytical presentation; corrections are interpreted as mutually exclusive to avoid overwriting the small-range result. This register-rank mechanism differs from Bloom bit membership.

source.citation: Alon, Matias and Szegedy (1999), The space complexity of approximating the frequency moments, Journal of Computer and System Sciences 58(1), 137–147, DOI 10.1006/jcss.1997.1545. Author-hosted 2002 manuscript section 2.2, Theorem 2.2, pp. 6–7: https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nogaa/PDFS/amsz4.pdf ; signed updates and explicit confidence parameters independently derived

mechanism_note: Expand the second and fourth powers of a signed projection. Terms with odd sign multiplicity vanish by four-wise independence; the fourth moment is Σ f_x⁴+6Σ_{x<y} f_x²f_y². Subtract F₂² to obtain the variance. Chebyshev bounds a block failure by 1/4 with q≥8/ε²; Hoeffding bounds the probability of at least half bad independent blocks by exp(−d/8). Unlike Count Sketch per-key signed bucket queries, the square of a scalar projection estimates a global quadratic functional; the nonlinear aggregation and target differ.

source.citation: Beyer, Gemulla, Haas, Reinwald and Sismanis (2009), Distinct-value synopses for multiset operations, Communications of the ACM 52(10), 87–95, Algorithm 1, sections 2 and 4.1, equation (2) and Theorem 2. DOI 10.1145/1562764.1562787. https://www.uni-mannheim.de/media/Einrichtungen/dws/Files_People/Profs/rgemulla/publications/beyer09distinct.pdf

mechanism_note: The kth order statistic has Beta(k,n−k+1) law. Integrating inverse powers against its density gives E[U_(k)^−r]=B(k−r,n−k+1)/B(k,n−k+1) for 0≤r<k. This yields the stated mean and variance, including n=k. The source discusses an exact n≤k branch; without an extra overflow indicator only n<k is detectable from S alone. The bottom-k union identity follows because any omitted value already has k smaller values in its own set. This retains numerical hash order statistics rather than HyperLogLog register ranks or reservoir samples of arrival positions.

source.citation: Nelson and Yu (2022), Optimal Bounds for Approximate Counting, section 1.2, p. 3 of author-hosted manuscript dated March 30 2022; attributes base-two counter to Morris (1978), Counting large numbers of events in small registers, Communications of the ACM 21(10), 840–842. https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~hy2/files/approx_counting.pdf

mechanism_note: Let Z=2^C. Conditional on Z, the next Z equals 2Z with probability 1/Z and Z otherwise. Thus E[Z_next|Z]=Z+1 and E[Z_next²|Z]=Z²+3Z. From Z₀=1 obtain E[Z_n]=n+1 and Var(Z_n)=n(n−1)/2 by summing the recurrences. Unlike KMV, this counts every arrival through state-dependent random increments, not distinct hash values. No separate admission for merely changing the exponential base.

source.citation: Datar, Gionis, Indyk and Motwani (2002), Maintaining Stream Statistics over Sliding Windows, SIAM Journal on Computing 31(6), 1794–1813, section 2.1, Fact 1, Invariant 2 and Algorithm INSERT; DOI 10.1137/S0097539701398363. https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/bruno.salvy/INF431/Projet-hyperloglog/INF431_-_Projet_Informatique_files/DatarGionisIndykMotwani2002.pdf

mechanism_note: The chronological groups contain consecutive arrivals of ones, so every retained bucket except the oldest lies wholly in the window. When B≥2 there are at least q buckets of each smaller power of two, since a merge leaves q of its size and expiration cannot reach smaller buckets while B remains. Thus C≥q(B−1)+1; absolute error ≤B/2 and B/[2(q(B−1)+1)]≤1/(q+1). A singleton oldest bucket is fully active. This uses deterministic age-aware coalescence, unlike Morris random increments. The source's printed invariant does not justify its sharper constant directly from the stated lower counts; this entry uses the weaker independently proved bound.

source.citation: Lemire (2006), Streaming Maximum-Minimum Filter Using No More than Three Comparisons per Element, Nordic Journal of Computing 13(4), 328–339; author manuscript arXiv:cs/0610046v5 (2007), section 4, monotonic wedge update, pp. 5–6. https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0610046

mechanism_note: If i<j and x_i≤x_j, every future trailing window that still contains i after j arrives also contains j. Thus i is dominated; equal values retain the more recent index. Expiry and dominance removal preserve the maximum at the front. This is an independently justified one-sided specialization of the wedge update; unlike the quantile marker estimator, it gives an exact extremum. No separate count for reversing comparisons to obtain a minimum.

source.citation: Fenwick (1994), A new data structure for cumulative frequency tables, Software: Practice and Experience 24(3), 327–336, Principles and Figures 4–5, pp. 328–331; DOI 10.1002/spe.4380240306. https://www.plouffe.fr/OEIS/archive_in_pdf/spe884.pdf

mechanism_note: Subtracting the lowest set bit partitions the prefix into disjoint consecutive dyadic intervals; adding that bit enumerates precisely the stored intervals containing the changed index. The update increases the lowest set-bit size until leaving the array. This is the one-based positive-index form with no stored index-zero frequency, unlike the paper's special zero slot. Distinct mutable dyadic representation, not chronological bucket coalescence or static pairwise summation.

source.citation: Carnegie Mellon University, 15-451 Algorithm Design and Analysis, Fall 2024, Range query data structures, sections 2–3 and 5.1, pp. 3–7 and 8–9. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~15451-f24/lectures/lecture06-range-queries.pdf

mechanism_note: Induction on interval splits proves every node stores the ordered fold, and disjoint query pieces concatenate in original order. Only the two boundary paths can contain partially intersecting nodes at each depth, yielding logarithmic combine count. Unlike Fenwick prefix differences, arbitrary monoid ranges require no inverse or commutativity. This is the independently derived unpadded inclusive formulation of the course's balanced half-open tree, not a new entry for each aggregate.

source.citation: Jeff Erickson (2025), Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 1: Range-Minimum Queries, section 1.1 Sparse Lookup Table, pp. 1–2 and footnote 2. https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/teaching/datastructures/notes/01-RMQ-LCA.pdf

mechanism_note: The two blocks cover the interval with contiguous overlap; the ordered product has form A⊗B⊗B⊗C, omitting empty outside pieces, and reduces to A⊗B⊗C by associativity and idempotence. Commutativity is not needed. The source treats minimum; this generalized ordered formulation is independently derived. Corrects the printed build loop upper endpoint to n−L+1. Distinct static overlapping-block lookup rather than disjoint mutable segment-tree traversal.

source.citation: Stajano and Sauerwald (2015), University of Cambridge Algorithms, 5.3 Disjoint Sets, slides 9–11; Tarjan (1975), Efficiency of a Good But Not Linear Set Union Algorithm, JACM 22(2), 215–225, DOI 10.1145/321879.321884 (bibliographic metadata and abstract checked). https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/1415/Algorithms/disjointsets.pdf

mechanism_note: Each parent edge strictly increases rank, excluding nonroot cycles. A root of rank r represents at least 2^r elements by induction on equal-rank mergers; compression changes no membership. The resulting logarithmic depth bound is independent of the cited stronger amortized theorem. This maintains arbitrary partitions, whereas Kruskal uses connectivity as a subroutine in a weighted graph algorithm.

source.citation: Demaine (2012), MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 15, sections 2.1–2.1.1, pp. 2–4. https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-851-advanced-data-structures-spring-2012/99d1ee86e7c3488b9a47174160776405_MIT6_851S12_L15.pdf

mechanism_note: The stack holds the increasing-key right spine. Replacing its popped suffix by the new node with the displaced subtree on the left preserves in-order index order and strict lexicographic heap order. These properties uniquely determine the tree by its minimum root and recursive subarrays. Each node is pushed once and popped at most once. Unlike a sliding-window deque, this construction retains child topology for all indices; unlike a sparse table it constructs an ordered tree rather than storing overlapping aggregates. Deterministic leftmost tie resolution is a specified convention.

source.citation: Demaine (2012), MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, Lecture 15, sections 1.3 and 4.2 (Algorithm B), pp. 2 and 7, CSAIL scribed notes. https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.851/fall17/scribe/lec15.pdf

mechanism_note: By induction T_{j,v}=P^{2^j}(v), extending P by an absorbing missing sentinel. Function composition adds iteration counts, so the binary expansion of k gives exactly P^k(v). Tree depth is at most n−1; the early large-distance check prevents missing levels. This is repeated parent-function composition, not overlapping range aggregation or union-find compression; it is not itself a lowest-common-ancestor algorithm. The source's section 4 height-difference notation is not used because height differences in branching trees need not equal edge distance.

source.citation: Knuth, Morris and Pratt (1977), Fast Pattern Matching in Strings, SIAM J. Comput. 6(2), 323–350, DOI 10.1137/0206024 (publisher abstract and metadata); Cornell CS 312 (2003), Lecture 27, KMP algorithm and prefix preprocessing. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs312/2003sp/lectures/lec27.html

mechanism_note: Every shorter viable alignment is a border of the already matched prefix; iterating proper borders enumerates these in decreasing length. The scan maintains the longest viable matched prefix, except that after emission it retains the longest proper border. Each fallback strictly decreases q and increases are at most one per processed symbol, giving linear total work. Cornell's prefix array is indexed by prefix length j, equivalent to π_{j−1}; the all-occurrences reset is independently derived. Distinct from suffix sorting and from Boyer–Moore majority cancellation, which is not string matching.

source.citation: Manber and Myers (1993), Suffix Arrays: A New Method for On-Line String Searches, SIAM J. Comput. 22(5), 935–948, DOI 10.1137/0222058 (bibliographic record and abstract); Kulcu, Advanced String Algorithms, §10.7.3 (pair-rank comparison-sort formulation). https://sercankulcu.github.io/files/algorithms/notes/Chapter_10_Advanced_String_Algorithms_Lecture_Notes.html

mechanism_note: Inductively ranks encode lexicographic order and equality of prefixes truncated at span h. Concatenating two adjacent truncated blocks gives the next prefix order; a missing second block ranks before any nonempty block. Distinct truncated prefixes fix their full suffix order, so early unique ranks are sufficient. When h≥n all distinct nonempty suffixes have been distinguished. Unlike KMP, this creates an index by repeated pair sorting rather than scanning a single fixed pattern. The comparison-sort specification is not a claim to implement the original paper's optimized sorting procedure.

source.citation: Wagner and Fischer (1974), The String-to-String Correction Problem, JACM 21(1), 168–173, DOI 10.1145/321796.321811 (bibliographic record and abstract); Cornell CS 4820 (2025), Dynamic Programming II: Edit Distance, and Dynamic Programming III: Analysis of Edit Distance (recurrence and boundaries). https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4820/2025sp/notes/07-ED-Analysis.pdf

mechanism_note: An optimal order-preserving alignment ends with a deletion, insertion or paired symbols. Under unit costs, repeated changes of one surviving symbol cannot beat direct substitution, and an inserted then deleted symbol can be omitted. Removing the final alignment operation leaves an optimal prefix subproblem; each predecessor also extends to a feasible alignment. Unlike exact pattern scanning and suffix ordering, this minimizes global edit cost.

source.citation: MIT 6.006 (Spring 2020), Lecture 16: Dynamic Programming Subproblems, pp. 2–3, longest common subsequence suffix recurrence and complexity; prefix form follows by reversing both sequences. https://live.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/28461a74f81101874a13d9679a40584d_MIT6_006S20_lec16.pdf

mechanism_note: If final symbols match an optimal common subsequence can be chosen to end at that pair; if unequal, at least one final position is unused. The score maximization is a material objective change within the same prefix-grid alignment family. With insertion/deletion cost one and unequal substitution cost two, D2(i,j)=i+j−2L(i,j); unequal substitution is replaceable by deletion plus insertion. This identity does not hold for unit substitutions (x=a,y=b gives D1=1, L=0). Conservatively count as a variant, not another distinct algorithm.

source.citation: Fredman (1975), On computing the length of longest increasing subsequences, Discrete Mathematics 11(1), 29–35, section 2, pp. 30–31, DOI 10.1016/0012-365X(75)90103-X; original distinct-input algorithm adapted to repeated values by lower-bound replacement. https://par.cse.nsysu.edu.tw/resource/paper/2014/140127/On%20computing%20the%20length%20of%20longest%20increasing%20subsequences.pdf

mechanism_note: Inductively, the minimal tail for length k+1 is strictly greater than the minimal tail for length k: remove the last value of a witness for length k+1. If j is the first tail at least x_i, a length j subsequence can extend to x_i (or start a singleton), but no longer one can do so. Shorter minimal tails cannot improve and only the j-th tail may improve or be appended. Equality therefore replaces rather than extends. This one-sequence ordered frontier differs from two-sequence prefix-grid dynamic programming.

source.citation: Manacher (1975), A New Linear-Time On-Line Algorithm for Finding the Smallest Initial Palindrome of a String, JACM 22(3), 346–351, DOI 10.1145/321892.321896 (metadata and abstract only); Princeton Algorithms, 4th ed., section 5.3 Manacher.java (transformed sequence mirror scan, indexed extract); Algorithms for Competitive Programming, Manacher's Algorithm (odd-radius explanation with exclusive endpoints). https://cp-algorithms.com/string/manacher.html

mechanism_note: Reflection in the known palindrome certifies the smaller of the reflected radius and r−i+1. If the reflected radius is strictly smaller, its stopping mismatch also reflects within the interval. Otherwise further successful comparisons extend the rightmost frontier; each advances a previously unverified right endpoint, and at most one unsuccessful comparison occurs per center. The inclusive zero-based formulation is independently derived from the exclusive-boundary invariant. Unlike exact pattern search or edit alignment, it reuses symmetry about changing centers.

source.citation: Gusfield (1997), Algorithms on Strings, Trees, and Sequences, Cambridge University Press, sections 1.3–1.5, especially p. 9, Algorithm Z; adapted from one-based inclusive intervals to zero-based half-open intervals. https://dmice.ohsu.edu/bedricks/courses/cs655/pdf/readings/gusfield_chap_1_2.pdf

mechanism_note: Inside the established prefix-copy interval, the earlier z value certifies the minimum of that value and the remaining interval length. If strictly smaller, the mismatch lies inside the known interval; otherwise successful comparisons extend the frontier. Outside the interval successes also advance the frontier; at most one failed comparison per index. Unlike the KMP recurrence, this measures prefix matches starting at each position rather than borders ending there. Conservatively grouped as a prefix-matching variant rather than counting closely related preprocessing separately.

source.citation: Aho and Corasick (1975), Efficient string matching: an aid to bibliographic search, Communications of the ACM 18(6), 333–340, DOI 10.1145/360825.360855 (metadata and abstract verified; original PDF retrieval failed). Stanford CS166, Tries and String Matching, sections Suffix Links, Constructing Output Links and The Complete Construction; dense transition bound independently derived. https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs166/cs166.1146/lectures/09/Small09.pdf

mechanism_note: The current state represents the longest suffix of processed text that is a prefix of some pattern. Failure moves to shorter represented suffixes. All matching patterns are terminal suffixes of that state, enumerated by terminal-only output links. Dense construction processes K transitions per state; output traversal visits exactly one terminal per report. A single-pattern trie specializes to the KMP failure mechanism; branching states and multiple terminal suffixes give the general automaton a distinct capability.

source.citation: Huffman (1952), A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes, Proceedings of the IRE 40(9), 1098–1101, Optimum Binary Code, pp. 1099–1100. https://cs.nyu.edu/home/people/in_memoriam/roweis/csc310-2006/extras/huffman_1952_minimum-redundancy-codes.pdf

mechanism_note: A positive-weight optimal full binary tree can place the two smallest weights at a deepest sibling pair by exchanges that do not increase cost. Contracting that pair gives a smaller prefix-code problem and adds exactly their weight sum to its cost. Induction yields greedy optimality for the stated objective. Entropy is an information measure, not this constructive tree algorithm.

source.citation: Ziv and Lempel (1978), Compression of individual sequences via variable-rate coding, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 24(5), 530–536, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1978.1055934 (bibliographic metadata checked). Goemans (2015), MIT 18.310A Lempel-Ziv codes, section 1, pp. LZ-1–LZ-2; explicit tagged terminal record is a specified framing adaptation. https://math.mit.edu/~goemans/18310S15/lempel-ziv-notes.pdf

mechanism_note: Prefix closure ensures that extending the longest matching phrase by the next symbol creates a new phrase. Each emitted normal token references an earlier dictionary entry, so decoder synchronization follows by induction; the terminal token handles a final already-known phrase. Unlike static multi-pattern matching, the dictionary grows from the input; unlike Huffman coding it adapts phrase boundaries and uses dictionary references.

source.citation: Howard and Vitter (1994), Arithmetic Coding for Data Compression, section II.A–B, manuscript p. 2, table 1 and figure 1. https://www.ittc.ku.edu/~jsv/Papers/HoV94.arithmetic_coding.pdf ; Witten, Neal and Cleary (1987), DOI 10.1145/214762.214771 (metadata and abstract checked). Least-grid exponent bound independently derived for explicitly framed points.

mechanism_note: At each step the subintervals partition the parent interval, and the selected width is the parent width times p_j. A dyadic grid with spacing no greater than the final width necessarily contains a point in that half-open interval. Known length resolves nested interval ambiguity. Unlike Huffman coding this assigns a joint sequence interval rather than independently concatenating symbol codewords.

source.citation: Welch (1984), A Technique for High-Performance Data Compression, Computer 17(6), 8–19, pp. 16–17, compression and decompression algorithms and special case. DOI 10.1109/MC.1984.1659158. https://courses.cs.duke.edu/spring03/cps296.5/papers/welch_1984_technique_for.pdf ; unbounded externally framed code list is a specified abstraction.

mechanism_note: LZW retains LZ78-style longest-phrase dictionary growth but starts from the full singleton alphabet and transmits indices alone instead of index/symbol pairs. The decoder is one insertion behind; only the next free code may refer to the immediately pending phrase, whose first symbol must equal that of the previous phrase. This material change in representation and synchronization justifies a variant, not another distinct algorithm count.

source.citation: Burrows and Wheeler (1994), A Block-sorting Lossless Data Compression Algorithm, SRC Research Report 124, section 2, pp. 2–4 (rotation and occurrence-ranked inverse). https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/2223/Bioinfo/papers/burrows_wheeler.pdf ; sentinel-only framing and single-cycle validity check independently derived from unique sentinel rotation order.

mechanism_note: Right-rotation of rows ending in the same symbol preserves their relative lexicographic order, giving LF by stable occurrence rank. A unique sentinel distinguishes every rotation and identifies the original row, so LF traverses one cycle of length N. Unlike suffix-array construction, the output is a reversible symbol permutation rather than an index; suffix ordering is a reusable subroutine, not an equivalent transform.

source.citation: Bentley, Sleator, Tarjan and Wei (1986), A Locally Adaptive Data Compression Scheme, Communications of the ACM 29(4), 320–330, p. 321, sections 2–3. DOI 10.1145/5684.5688. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~sleator/papers/adaptive-data-compression.pdf ; fixed shared alphabet and zero-based ranks are an explicit restricted convention, not the full new-word or integer coding scheme.

mechanism_note: The state is an ordering of fixed symbols by recency, rather than an expanding phrase dictionary or a global rotation permutation. Rank emission plus deterministic list update is invertible with shared state, and can be composed with the Burrows–Wheeler transform without being equivalent to it.

source.citation: Elias (1975), Universal codeword sets and representations of the integers, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 21(2), 194–203, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1975.1055349 (bibliographic metadata checked; original full text not reviewed). CMU 15-853 Algorithms in the Real World, Data compression continued, slide 43, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~15853-f19/slides/compress3.pdf (uses opposite unary polarity; only the unary prefix is complemented here).

mechanism_note: The unary header uniquely specifies the number of remaining binary bits, so different header lengths disagree before either can be a prefix, and equal header lengths imply equal total codeword length. Unlike a fitted Huffman tree, no symbol probability table or finite alphabet tree is needed.

source.citation: Elias (1975), Universal codeword sets and representations of the integers, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 21(2), 194–203, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1975.1055349 (bibliographic metadata checked; original full text not reviewed). Mansouri (2022), University of Southern Maine, Introduction to Information Retrieval, Session 5, slide 35, https://cs.usm.maine.edu/~behrooz.mansouri/courses/Slides_IR_22/Introduction%20to%20Information%20Retrieval%20--%20Session%205%20-%20Indexing%20%26%20Ranking.pdf (gamma-coded length followed by binary remainder; here leading-zero gamma convention).

mechanism_note: Gamma's unary length header is replaced by a gamma code for L, while the binary remainder is unchanged. Prefix-freeness follows from gamma header prefix-freeness and the fixed remaining length once L is decoded. This nested header is a material variant of gamma rather than an independent algorithm count.

source.citation: Treib (2014), GPU-Based Compression for Large-Scale Visualization, TU München dissertation, §2.1.3, p. 15, https://mediatum.ub.tum.de/doc/1190931/939759.pdf (quotient and truncated-binary remainder; unary polarity complemented here). Golomb (1966), Run-Length Encodings, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 12(3), 399–401, bibliographic citation checked via Kiely; original full paper not reviewed.

mechanism_note: The unary quotient identifies a disjoint block of m integers; truncated binary distinguishes residues using t short leaves and m−t long leaves. The remainder Kraft sum is t·2^(−(b−1))+(m−t)·2^(−b)=1 for m>1; the unary-only case is separate. This quotient/remainder construction is distinct from Elias length headers and fitted finite Huffman trees.

Treib (2014), §2.1.3, https://mediatum.ub.tum.de/doc/1190931/939759.pdf (power-of-two restriction). Rice (1979), Some Practical Universal Noiseless Coding Techniques, JPL 79-22, NASA document 19790014634 (metadata reviewed; original full report not reviewed).

mechanism_note: When m=2^k and k>0, the Golomb threshold t=0 and b=k, so all residues have k bits; k=0 gives the same unary-only special case. This is a material restricted variant, not an additional distinct algorithm.

source.citation: Deutsch (1996), RFC 1951, DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification, §§2 and 3.2.3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1951.html (literal and distance/length token model, overlapping copies; this specification generalizes bounds and uses its own greedy rule and framing). Ziv and Lempel (1977), A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 23(3), 337–343, DOI 10.1109/TIT.1977.1055714 (metadata and abstract reviewed; original full paper not reviewed).

mechanism_note: Each copied symbol references an already produced symbol because d≥1, including within overlapping copies; induction on decoded length proves lossless reconstruction. Unlike LZ78, no persistent phrase dictionary or phrase-index insertion is required; references are bounded relative positions. This is a distinct sliding-window mechanism.

source.citation: Kulcu, Algorithms Lecture Notes, Chapter 9: String Matching and Compression, §9.8.1, https://sercankulcu.github.io/files/algorithms/notes/Chapter_09_String_Matching_and_Compression_Lecture_Notes.html (maximal runs and count-symbol pairs). TIFF Image File Format Rev. 4.0, Appendix C, https://cool.culturalheritage.org/bytopic/imaging/std/tiff4.html (historical PackBits repeat packets; not the same wire format).

mechanism_note: Run boundaries occur exactly at unequal adjacent symbols; the unique maximal-run partition is recovered from its ordered symbols and lengths. This is not Golomb coding of integers, nor general LZ77 substring substitution; although long constant runs can be represented using distance-one LZ77 references, the canonical run partition is a different sequence representation.

source.citation: University of Pennsylvania, CIS 1210, Spring 2025, Recitation 7, Kahn’s algorithm, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis1210/current/recitations/fa25_rec_7_sols.pdf (retrieved text; screenshot unavailable). Original Kahn (1962) DOI 10.1145/368996.369025 retained as unverified locator.

mechanism_note: Maintains indegree of the unprocessed induced graph. Every nonempty finite DAG has a source; each emitted vertex precedes all its unprocessed successors. If no source remains, following predecessors in the finite residual graph yields a cycle. Distinct from shortest-path and spanning-forest objectives.

source.citation: Cornell CS 4120 (Spring 2023), Iterative solving, Tarjan’s algorithm, https://courses.cs.cornell.edu/cs4120/2023sp/notes/iterative/index.html. Original Tarjan (1972) DOI 10.1137/0201010 retained as unverified locator.

mechanism_note: The root condition identifies a maximal mutually reachable group; active-stack bookkeeping distinguishes completed components. Floyd–Warshall computes pairwise paths rather than this linear-time partition; Kahn orders the resulting condensation DAG, not the cyclic graph itself.

source.citation: MIT 6.854, Strongly Polynomial Flow Algorithms, Scribe Notes #7, §2, https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.854/21/Scribe/s7-blockingFlows/unit-capacity.html. Edmonds and Karp (1972) DOI 10.1145/321694.321699 retained as unverified locator.
